cands.bio: Republican state representative for Alabama House District 93 since 1994. He is vice president of Clouse Marketing Company and worked in the family oil distribution business. He chaired the House Ways and Means General Fund Committee for over a decade and now chairs the Transportation, Utilities and Infrastructure Committee.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists the Alabama Tea Party Express as having endorsed Clouse. The page gives no date. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for the 2026 race.

cands.gaps: We found nothing from Clouse's own statements or record that speaks to data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, donor money, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 or 2022 candidate surveys. No documented public stances on data centers or development turned up. No controversies turned up in the pages reviewed. His birthplace and upbringing in Ozark come only from his own campaign website, with no independent source. His campaign site credits him with local projects such as a forensics lab and a mental health crisis center, but it does not say what he did to bring them about, so we left them out. The sources do not say whether Clouse Marketing Company and the family oil distribution business are the same company.

qual.background: Alabama House member since 1994 (32 years). He chaired the Ways and Means General Fund Committee, which writes the state General Fund budget, and works in the family business as vice president of Clouse Marketing Company.
qual.why: Over three decades of legislative service with direct involvement in writing the state budget, plus business experience, fits the high band for a job that is writing law and the budget.
